evals.prompt: Add a CancelOrder command and handler to the supplied TypeScript app using its installed @cqrsx/core. Cancellation must call the OrderEntity cancellation behavior before saving. Wire it into startup with an injected repository and include a callable dispatch example. Test successful persistence and rejection of a shipped order with an in-memory repository.
evals.expected_output: A co-located command and handler with registration and exec dispatch; domain entity owns the rule.
expectations: Command and handler are in the same file.
The handler invokes domain behavior before persistence.
The command is dispatched with cqrsx.exec.

evals.prompt: The supplied TypeScript app needs a filtered invoice list with its own result shape. Add the query path using the installed @cqrsx/core and the IInvoiceProjection port, accepting open or paid status. Wire it at startup, show dispatch, and test filtering without changing the domain model.
evals.expected_output: A Query<TResult> and co-located handler returning a read model, with no domain mutation.
expectations: The query extends Query with an explicit result type.

evals.prompt: Using the installed @cqrsx/core in this app, add a RecordHeartbeatCommand carrying a source string and a HeartbeatRecordedEvent carrying the same source. A command handler should write heartbeat:<source> through the IAuditLog port, then publish the event. An event handler should write observed:<source> through that port. Wire and test dispatch through the real bus, including that an audit failure prevents event publication. Keep port contracts compatible.
evals.expected_output: Co-located messages and handlers using compatible exec signatures, explicit register/exec/publish, and failure-safe orchestration.
expectations: Each command/event lives with its own handler and implements the installed ICommandHandler or IEventHandler exec signature without a wrapper parameter that breaks bus dispatch.
The command is invoked with cqrsx.exec and the event is emitted with cqrsx.publish; both handlers are registered.
The existing IAuditLog.append(entry: string) contract remains callable directly without a breaking object wrapper.
An in-memory audit fake verifies heartbeat then observed entries through real bus dispatch.
A rejected heartbeat audit write rejects dispatch and no observed event entry is written.
